children: Wall Street
the week mixed as a sharp spike in volatility reflected fresh tech struggles, while investors continued to digest hotter-than-expected CPI data and the latest bank earnings.
State Street Financial Sel Sec SPDR ETF
advanced 0.68% from the previous week to close at $55.90.
Among megacap stocks, Toronto-Dominion Bank
led the weekly gainers, adding 3.51% to close at $124.61.
The week saw the Canadian lender's U.S. unit
TD Credit Assist, an AI capability that reduces the time required to prepare a first-draft commercial credit analysis from up to three working days to less than 30 minutes.

"By reducing time spent on manual preparation, our credit professionals can focus more of their time on understanding the client, assessing risk, and moving opportunities forward," said Jill Gateman, Head of Commercial Banking, TD Bank U.S.
Berkshire Hathaway (
) (BRK.B) followed with 1.95% and 1.91% gains to $813,595.00 and $542.19, respectively.
B shares touched a new high on Wednesday, an indication that investors have become more confident in Greg Abel, who succeeded Warren Buffett as CEO on Jan. 1, 2026.
HSBC Holdings
was the top decliner, retreating 4.11% to $90.68.

The global lender is set to post its third-quarter financial results next week; and even as earnings are expected to come in strong on the back of higher interest rates and resilient Asian wealth management fees, mounting cost pressures and regulatory uncertainty from China may impact stock prices.
Japanese lender Mitsubishi UFJ
(-3.70% W/W to $21.07) was the next on the list.

The week saw Japanese banks, along with other organizations, temporarily take digital services offline in response to certain security vulnerabilities in the PHP programming language. Separately, the Bank of Japan warned of rising risks from AI, including growing cybersecurity threats and potential ‌market shocks, that could impact the country's banking system.
Globe Life
was among the top largecap losers, retreating 8.28% week-over-week to $154.79.
The life and health insurer was downgraded to Neutral from Overweight at Piper Sandler after reporting third-quarter earnings below Wall Street estimates this week.
First Citizens Bancshares
led the gainers, advancing 11.87% to $2,375.84. The stock was gaining after posting better-than-expected Q3 earnings and announcing a new $1.2B stock buyback program.
Blackstone
added 10.66% from the prior week to $117.97 even as Q3 earnings fell short of consensus.
TransUnion
(+9.99% W/W to $81.48) extended gains from the previous week, when a general strength was seen across the broader credit reporting sector.
Among midcap stocks, UWM Holdings

(+38.10% W/W to $1.45) was the top advancer. The mortgage finance provider reported its preliminary unaudited results for the quarter ended September 30, as part of which it said it expects to report total revenue between $800M and $825M, above the consensus of $651.35M.
FirstCash Holdings
(-19.75% W/W to $172.75) was the top loser in the category despite a Q3 beat and dividend raise.
Better Home & Finance
(+68.04% W/W to $16.72), Chaince Digital
(+26.41% W/W to $8.76), Stewart Information Services
(-16.12% W/W to $44.07), and Gemini Space Station
(-14.29% W/W to $3.06) were the notable smallcap movers.

title: Berkshire Hathaway, Blackstone in gainers; HSBC, Globe Life among losers: week's financials wrap
